about: Reference recordings of wild wood ducks (Aix sponsa), all from xeno-canto. Licenses were checked on each recording's own page on 2026-11-13. trimStartSec/trimEndSec are seconds in the original file as downloaded. Each clip keeps at least 0.3 s before the call for the noise floor. Calls were classified by measurement against the cited call definitions in callDefinitions; uncertain clips say so in notes (and uncertain: true). Every recording used says 'Playback used: no' on its page. Wood ducks are kept in waterfowl collections and have escaped and feral birds in Europe: only recordings from the native range (United States, Canada) were used, and recordings whose page mentions an escaped, feral, captive, domestic or fed bird, a park or a waterfowl collection were left out (e.g. XC522565 'Feral population', XC855694 'certainly escaped', XC177728 Powderhorn Park, XC754267 'along an urban park'). Originals with samples at full scale were rejected (XC724843). Classification is by spectrogram and measurement; no expert or recordist confirmed it.

callDefinitions.readVia: shortcut: all sources were read through web-search excerpts, because this build environment's network blocks allaboutbirds.org, birdsoftheworld.org and ducks.org (checked 2026-11-13). Quotes below are from those excerpts. Re-read the pages directly when next editing this text (owner check in docs/STATUS.md).

bow-sounds.title: Birds of the World (Cornell Lab of Ornithology), Wood Duck, Sounds and Vocal Behavior

calls.name: Hen flush call ('oo-eek')
calls.definition: Females make a loud 'oo-eek, oo-eek' when disturbed and taking flight (All About Birds).
calls.use: When disturbed and taking flight (All About Birds). The female's loud call is also used to find the mate after separation and to keep contact in flight (Birds of the World).
calls.classifyBy: a series of 2 or more harmonic notes, each about 0.1-0.6 s, fundamental 1.3-1.7 kHz rising within the note, from a female flushing or in flight (page sex, type or remarks); isolated from other calls by >= 0.3 s before the first note.

calls.name: Drake whistle
calls.definition: The male has a thin, rising and falling, zeeting whistle (All About Birds).
calls.use: The sources read do not say when drakes give it.
calls.classifyBy: one thin tonal note, 0.2-0.6 s, rising in pitch (with or without a fall at the end), from a male (page sex or remarks).

notIncluded.hen-squeal: No source read separates a hen 'squeal' from the flush call. Ducks Unlimited, Call in the Wood Ducks (https://ducks.org/hunting/duck-calling/call-in-the-wood-ducks, search excerpt) mentions the 'wheet-wheet' squeal a wood duck makes in flight, without saying which sex or whether it is the flush call; it may be the same call. Not a separate call here.
notIncluded.hen-reek: Several pages label short, broadband female notes 'reek' or alarm (XC512410, XC935141, XC817851, XC1145506); no source excerpt read defines this call, so it is not included and these recordings are not used.
